title: Fall Risk Assessment in Older Adults

evidenceAudit.scope: Adult aged 65 and over, or a younger adult with frailty, seen in a Saudi primary health centre, clinic or hospital: ask about falls, stratify the risk as low, intermediate or high using fall history, injury, frailty and gait speed, carry out a multifactorial assessment for high-risk patients (gait and balance, medicines, blood pressure on standing, heart rhythm, vision, cognition, feet, home, nutrition and vitamin D), and plan multidomain prevention. Uses the 2022 World Falls Guidelines and Saudi studies. Not for the acute management of a fracture or head injury.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-14.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: No Saudi national falls prevention guideline was found; the 2022 World Falls Guidelines (an international consensus by 96 experts from 39 countries) are used as the main source and are applied to Saudi practice without local validation.

Saudi data used: a cross-sectional online survey of 403 community-dwelling adults aged 60 and over in Jeddah (47.4% had fallen; 36.2% of fallers were injured and 25.3% had fractures) and the Saudi National Survey for Elderly Health (13% reported falls; benzodiazepine users had twice the risk). Both rely on self-report, and the Jeddah sample was recruited online.
Saudi emergency room fall data (a 2023 online survey of 1,763 people, mostly young adults) were read but are not used because they do not describe older patients.

The guideline's gait speed cut-off is below 0.8 metres per second and Timed Up and Go above 15 seconds; its definition of orthostatic hypotension is not stated in the text read, so no numerical blood pressure threshold is given in this topic.

Vitamin D: the guideline says supplementation should be reserved for people at risk of deficiency and that 800 to 1,000 IU daily is reasonable; it gives no Saudi dose. The product label read is a Canadian liquid supplement (1,000 IU per drop) and the contraindications come from a United States prescription ergocalciferol label; the Saudi supplement register and local products were not checked.
Local data on vitamin D deficiency in Saudi older adults, and the Saudi thresholds for treating it, were not found or read.

The guideline recommends a structured tool (STOPPFall or STEADI) for fall-risk-increasing medicines; the tools themselves were not read, so drug-by-drug advice for sedatives, antihypertensives and others is not written, and no dose-reduction schedule is given.
Frailty tools (Clinical Frailty Scale, frailty phenotype) are named by the guideline; the cut-offs were not read here.
Exercise programmes, home hazard assessment tools and orthostatic hypotension treatments are described in outline only; no drug regimen for orthostatic hypotension was reviewed.
Figures were read by automated extraction of web and label text; spot-check each figure and dose against the source during clinical review.

pathophysiology.summary: Falls come from the combination of many risk factors, so the guidelines advise multifactorial assessment for high-risk people rather than one test (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Section Multifactorial falls risk assessment). Gait speed below 0.8 metres per second predicts falls (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Section Assessment and algorithm flow, Recommendation details). Medicines that increase fall risk (psychotropic and cardiovascular drugs among them) are a modifiable cause (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Section Medication assessment). Postural blood pressure drops, rhythm disturbance and unexplained falls with transient loss of consciousness may be syncope (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Section Cardiovascular assessment). Vision, hearing, cognition, foot problems, urinary urgency, fear of falling and home hazards add to the risk (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Table 4). A fall may be the presenting feature of acute illness such as pneumonia or painless heart attack (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Section Multifactorial falls risk assessment).

symptoms: One or more falls in the past 12 months, with details of circumstances and consequences (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Section Opportunistic case-finding).
Dizziness, loss of consciousness, unsteadiness when standing or walking, or worry about falling (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Section Opportunistic case-finding).
Limiting usual activities because of fear of falling (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Section Concerns about falling and falls).
Urinary urgency or incontinence, pain, low mood (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Table 4).
physicalSigns: Gait speed below 0.8 metres per second over 4 metres, or Timed Up and Go above 15 seconds (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Section Assessment and algorithm flow, Recommendation details).
Drop in blood pressure on standing with symptoms (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Table 4).
Poor vision, hearing loss, inappropriate footwear or foot problems (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Table 4).
Cognitive impairment or delirium (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Table 4).
Weak muscle strength or sarcopenia (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Table 4).
redFlags: Fall with an injury needing medical treatment: manage the injury and treat as high risk (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Section Older adults presenting with falls or related injuries).
Lying on the floor for an hour or more unable to get up (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Section Older adults presenting with falls or related injuries).
Fall with suspected transient loss of consciousness: evaluate as syncope (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Section Cardiovascular assessment).
Two or more falls in 12 months, or known frailty: high risk (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Section Older adults presenting with falls or related injuries).
Fall with new confusion or fever: look for acute illness such as pneumonia or delirium (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Section Multifactorial falls risk assessment).
precipitants: Older age (95 to 104 years), female sex, antihypertensive medicines, history of hip or knee replacement and presence of a caregiver were associated with previous falls in Jeddah (Jeddah falls study, Section Results).
Stroke, osteoporosis, lower limb weakness, dizziness, wheelchair use and fear of stumbling were associated with falls (Jeddah falls study, Section Results).
Benzodiazepine use: relative risk of falls about 2 in Saudi older adults (Saudi National Survey benzodiazepine study, Section Results).
Antidepressants, laxatives, low body mass index, mild cognitive impairment, high door steps and poor lighting (Saudi National Survey benzodiazepine study, Section Results).
Care home or hospital residence: all residents should be regarded as high risk (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Section Key messages).

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: A clear trip or slip, no dizziness or gait problem; address the hazard and reassess (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Section Environmental assessment).
Loss of consciousness, palpitations, postural symptoms; evaluate as syncope (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Section Cardiovascular assessment).
New confusion, fever or atypical presentation of pneumonia or heart attack (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Section Multifactorial falls risk assessment).
Recent start or increase of sedatives, antihypertensives or other fall-risk-increasing drugs (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Section Medication assessment).
Parkinson disease, stroke, neuropathy, sarcopenia or osteoarthritis causing gait and balance problems (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Table 4).

clinicalManagement.title: Ask about falls
actions: Ask every older adult at least once a year whether they fell in the past 12 months, and about frequency, circumstances and consequences (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Section Opportunistic case-finding).
If time allows ask about dizziness, loss of consciousness, gait or balance problems and fear of falling (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Section Opportunistic case-finding).

Use the three key questions where available: fallen in the past year, unsteady when standing or walking, worries about falling (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Section Assessment and algorithm flow, Recommendation details).

clinicalManagement.title: Test gait and stratify the risk
actions: Offer an objective gait and balance test to anyone who answers yes; gait speed over 4 metres is preferred, Timed Up and Go is an alternative (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Section Opportunistic case-finding; Section Assessment and algorithm flow).
Classify as low, intermediate or high risk (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Section Assessment and algorithm flow, Recommendation details).
In care homes and hospitals treat all as high risk and go straight to multifactorial assessment (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Section Key messages).
Treat a fall with suspected syncope as a syncope evaluation (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Section Cardiovascular assessment).

clinicalManagement.title: Low risk: educate and review
actions: Give advice on safe mobility, physical activity and nutrition including vitamin D intake (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Section Management of older adults at low fall risk).
Reassess each year (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Section Assessment and algorithm flow, Recommendation details).

clinicalManagement.title: Intermediate risk: strength and balance exercise
actions: Offer individualised exercise, three or more sessions a week, progressed for at least 12 weeks, including balance and functional exercise; Tai Chi or strength training when feasible (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Section Interventions for community dwelling older adults at intermediate fall risk).
Refer to a physiotherapist where available (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Section Assessment and algorithm flow, Recommendation details).

clinicalManagement.title: High risk: multifactorial assessment
actions: Assess history of falls, gait and balance, muscle strength, medicines, orthostatic blood pressure and cardiovascular status, dizziness, vision and hearing, feet and footwear, cognition and delirium, mood, continence, pain, fear of falling, nutrition and vitamin D, and the home (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Table 4).
Review every medicine with a structured tool such as STOPPFall or STEADI (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Table 4).
Ask what the person thinks about falls and what they want from care (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Section Incorporating the perspective of the older adult).

clinicalManagement.title: Offer multidomain interventions
actions: Include strength and balance exercise, medicine review, management of orthostatic hypotension and cardiovascular disease, treatment of underlying disease, vision and hearing, foot care and footwear, vitamin D when at risk of deficiency, nutrition, continence care, support for fear of falling, education and home modification (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Section Multidomain interventions for community dwelling older adults at high fall risk).
Deprescribe fall-risk-increasing drugs; in long-term care this should always be part of the plan (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Section Medication assessment).
Do not use physical restraints in care homes (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Section Key messages).

clinicalManagement.title: Review and post-fall assessment
actions: After a fall in hospital or a care home, do a post-fall assessment of the mechanism, injury and precipitating factors (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Section Falls in hospitals and care homes).
Review the plan and reassess risk; low-risk patients are reassessed yearly (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Section Assessment and algorithm flow, Recommendation details).

regimens.indication: Reducing falls in older adults at risk of vitamin D deficiency as part of a multidomain programme
regimens.patientGroup: Older adults who are frail, housebound or in care homes, or have a measured low 25-hydroxyvitamin D
regimens.dose: 800 to 1,000 IU a day (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Section Vitamin D interventions); with the 1,000 IU per drop liquid, 1 drop once a day (Vitamin D3 drops label, Directions for use). Doses of 2,000 or 4,000 IU a day were not harmful in the VITAL trial (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Section Vitamin D interventions). Dilution and preparation: no dilution needed; the drop can be taken directly or mixed with a beverage (Vitamin D3 drops label, Directions for use).
regimens.route: Oral; take the drop from the supplied dropper directly or mix into a drink; store upright at 15 to 25 degrees Celsius with the seal intact (Vitamin D3 drops label, Storage and Warnings)
regimens.duration: Long-term while the risk of deficiency persists; supplementation is not advised for everyone because universal supplementation does not prevent falls (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Section Vitamin D interventions)
adjustments: Not routinely recommended for older adults who are not at risk of deficiency; ≥1,000 IU a day did not reduce falls in those with levels of 30 ng/mL or above (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Section Vitamin D interventions).
In care home residents give vitamin D with calcium- and protein-rich food as part of a multidomain programme (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Section Falls in hospitals and care homes).
Count vitamin D from fortified foods, supplements and prescription sources and avoid duplication; individualise the dose (Ergocalciferol label, Precautions, General).
Pregnancy is not relevant to this age group; vitamin D above recommended levels should be avoided in pregnancy (Ergocalciferol label, Pregnancy).
In older people start at the low end of dosing because of lower kidney, liver and heart function (Ergocalciferol label, Geriatric Use).
Mineral oil reduces absorption; thiazide diuretics with high-dose vitamin D can cause hypercalcaemia (Ergocalciferol label, Drug Interactions).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Serum calcium if a high therapeutic dose is used (Ergocalciferol label, Precautions, General).
Thirst, passing urine at night, nausea or confusion that could mean excess vitamin D (Ergocalciferol label, Adverse Reactions).
Falls, gait speed and 25-hydroxyvitamin D at review (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Table 4).
contraindications: Abnormal sensitivity to the toxic effects of vitamin D, or hypervitaminosis D (Ergocalciferol label, Contraindications).

branches.label: Vitamin D for older adults at risk of deficiency
branches.entryCriteria: Older adult at risk of vitamin D deficiency (for example frail, housebound, care home resident, or measured level below 30 ng/mL) with normal serum calcium and no hypercalcaemia, malabsorption or vitamin D toxicity.

medicationPlan.note: Fall prevention is mainly by assessment, exercise, medicine review and home changes; the only medicine written here is vitamin D, and only for people at risk of deficiency. Deprescribing is a review process and is not written as a regimen. Dose and use come from the World Falls Guidelines; product, dilution and administration come from the supplement label and class cautions from the ergocalciferol label. SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: No falls, or one non-severe fall with no gait or balance problem; give education and exercise advice and reassess every year (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Section Assessment and algorithm flow, Recommendation details).
One non-severe fall with gait or balance problems; offer strength and balance exercise or physiotherapy (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Section Assessment and algorithm flow, Recommendation details).

A fall with injury needing treatment, two or more falls in 12 months, frailty, lying an hour or more, or suspected transient loss of consciousness; offer multifactorial assessment (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Section Older adults presenting with falls or related injuries).
Below 0.8 metres per second suggests higher risk; Timed Up and Go above 15 seconds is an alternative (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Section Assessment and algorithm flow, Recommendation details).
Regard all as high risk; do not use scored screening tools in hospital (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Section Key messages).
Ask about falls in the past 12 months at least once a year at any contact (World Falls Guidelines 2022, Section Opportunistic case-finding).

values: No falls, or one non-severe fall with no gait or balance problem

teaching.scope: Adult aged 65 and over, or a younger adult with frailty, seen in a Saudi primary health centre, clinic or hospital: ask about falls, stratify the risk as low, intermediate or high using fall history, injury, frailty and gait speed, carry out a multifactorial assessment for high-risk patients (gait and balance, medicines, blood pressure on standing, heart rhythm, vision, cognition, feet, home, nutrition and vitamin D), and plan multidomain prevention. Uses the 2022 World Falls Guidelines and Saudi studies. Not for the acute management of a fracture or head injury.
learningObjectives: Ask about falls at least once a year and test gait speed in anyone who has fallen or is unsteady.
Classify risk as low, intermediate or high; do a multifactorial assessment for high risk.
Review medicines, orthostatic blood pressure, vision, feet, cognition, home and vitamin D.
Offer exercise three times a week for at least 12 weeks and reassess.
pitfalls: Not asking about falls because patients do not mention them.
Using a scored screening tool for hospital inpatients.
Prescribing sedatives without a falls review.
keyPoints: Treat all care home residents and hospital inpatients as high risk.
Suspected syncope needs syncope evaluation, not only falls assessment.
Give vitamin D only to those at risk of deficiency.
Benzodiazepines about doubled fall risk in Saudi older adults.

patientEducation: Falls are common: almost half of older adults in a Jeddah survey had fallen in the past year, and one in four of those had a fracture.
Tell your doctor about every fall, even if you were not hurt.
Exercise that challenges balance, three times a week for at least 3 months, lowers the risk of falling.
Ask your pharmacist or doctor to review your medicines, especially sleeping tablets and blood pressure medicines.
Stand up slowly, wear shoes that fit, check your eyes and ears, and keep floors and stairs clear and well lit.
Have a plan to get help if you fall and cannot get up.
lifestyleAndDiet: Keep active with walking, Tai Chi or strengthening exercises recommended by your clinician.
Remove loose rugs, fix lighting, add bathroom rails and a non-slip mat.
Eat enough protein, calcium-rich foods and take vitamin D only if advised.
mdtReferrals: Primary care physician or geriatrician; nurse; physiotherapist; occupational therapist for home assessment; pharmacist for medicine review; optometrist; podiatrist; dietitian; cardiologist for syncope; social worker.
dischargeCriteria: Risk category recorded; assessment findings and plan documented; medicines reviewed and changes explained; exercise or physiotherapy referral made; home assessment arranged; written falls advice given; follow-up booked.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Low risk: reassess every year. Intermediate risk: review after the exercise programme (at least 12 weeks). High risk: review the multidomain plan at 3 months and after any fall.
